YOUTH GROUPS HOLD 'GHOST HUNTING' PROTEST VS FLOOD CONTROL SCAM

Youth Against Kurakot (YaK!), Akbayan Party, and allied groups on Friday staged a creative protest dubbed "Ghost Hunting in Pasig" outside the headquarters of St. Gerrard Construction, a firm linked to the Discaya family.

The demonstrators said the action symbolized a call to "exorcise" corruption in the national budget and demand accountability from Sarah Discaya, her contractor cohorts, and public officials allegedly involved in the trillion-peso flood control scam.

Khylla Meneses, Akbayan Youth Secretary General and YaK! Co-Convenor, said Filipinos—especially the youth—are haunted by billions lost to ghost projects.

"We must exorcise corruption in government once and for all," she said, stressing that stolen funds should have been used to build classrooms for students.

Akbayan President Rafaela "Paeng" David added that the Discayas are "just the tip of the iceberg," saying their alleged collusion with politicians must be fully exposed. She also called for the immediate freezing of their assets.

"Ninakaw nila ito mula sa taumbayan at dapat maibalik ito sa kaban ng bayan," David said.

The groups vowed to sustain peaceful protests and push for key reforms, including the passage of the Freedom of Information (FOI) Bill, the SALN Disclosure Bill, and greater transparency in the budget process.
